title: Running a company
subtitle: set up, expand, headquarters, clients
summary: Describe a company - how it started, what it produces, where its offices are and how it has grown.

lesson.heading: achieve and a great deal
lesson.text: If you **achieve** something, you have been successful in something that needed a lot of work and effort. The noun is **achievement**. **A great deal** means a lot.

examples.text: Writing a book has been my greatest **achievement**.
The company has **achieved a great deal** in a short period of time.
The firm has expanded **a great deal** in the last 20 years.

lesson.heading: Starting and growing a business
rows: started (used about a company or organisation)
a plan of what you hope to achieve
how good or bad something is
when more people want to buy something

lesson.heading: Denham Farm Bakery
lesson.text: Denham Farm Bakery is a family business. Three generations of the family are **currently** working there with a team of 90 **employees**. A **bakery** is a place where bread and cakes are made or sold.

examples.text: The company was **set up** in 1991.
Their **aim** was to produce a **variety** of bread of the highest **quality**.
There was a growing **demand** for organic products in the 1990s.
They soon became **experts** in the field of organic bread-making.
examples.note: an expert is a person with skill or knowledge in something

lesson.note: Currently means 'now, at the moment'. Do not use actually for this.

lesson.heading: How the company works
lesson.text: The company is **run** (organised and controlled) from a factory in Ilminster, where the bread is baked **daily** and then **delivered** to shops across the south-west of England.

examples.text: The company is **run** from a factory in Ilminster.
The bread is baked **daily**.
The bread is **delivered** to shops across the south-west.
The **firm** has **expanded** a great deal, but it is still a family business.

lesson.heading: A view of a company
rows: in the past but not now
the place where the main office is
an office that is part of the company
people who pay someone for a service
the way that people think of someone

lesson.heading: Morgan & Stenson
lesson.text: Morgan & Stenson are a firm of **accountants**: people who control a person's or a company's money. They were **formerly** Stenson & Son, but were **taken over** by JS Morgan five years ago.

examples.text: James Morgan **took up the position** of senior partner.
The **headquarters** of the firm are in Newcastle, but they have five other **branches**.
He is a **former** owner of a football club, with many **contacts** in the football world.
The company **attracted a lot of attention** when it advertised on local TV.
It was his **ambition** to change the **image** that people have of accountants.

lesson.heading: Three pairs to be careful with
lesson.text: We usually say **ex-wife** or **ex-boyfriend**, but **former president**, **former career**, **former banker**. Shops and organisations have **customers**; lawyers and accountants have **clients**. We **take up** a job or activity, but we **set up** a company.

examples.text: She's my **ex-wife**; we got divorced last year.
George Bush is **a former** president of America.
The shop assistant was serving a **customer**.
Her law firm has many famous **clients**.
When did you **take up** tennis? When did they **set up** the company?

lesson.text: Use *currently* for 'now, at the moment' - not *actually*, which means 'in fact'.

exercises.prompt: Which of these words refer to people?
'The food is delivered every day.' Another way to say this is: The food is delivered ___.
'There is a real need for food of this quality.' Another way to say this is: There is a real ___ for food of this quality.
exercises.explanation: Demand is when a lot of people want to buy something.

exercises.prompt: 'Our plan is to open another branch.' Another way to say this is: Our ___ is to open another branch.
exercises.explanation: An aim is a plan of what you hope to achieve.

exercises.prompt: 'We have 25 workers.' Another way to say this is: We have 25 ___.
exercises.explanation: Employees are the people a company employs.

exercises.prompt: 'I started the business ten years ago.' Another way to say this is: I ___ the business ten years ago.
exercises.explanation: We set up a company or an organisation.

exercises.prompt: 'Their main offices are in Sheffield.' Another way to say this is: Their ___ are in Sheffield.
exercises.explanation: The headquarters is the place where the main office is.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word: Marcel used to work here, but he's ___ working abroad.
exercises.explanation: Currently means now, at the moment.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word: When did you ___ tennis?
exercises.explanation: We take up a job or an activity, but we set up a company.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word: Are they planning to ___ the company?
exercises.explanation: To take over a company means to get control of it.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word: She's my ___ wife; we got divorced last year.
exercises.explanation: We say ex-wife and ex-boyfriend, but former president and former banker.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with the word that rewrites it.

pairs.left: I know a lot of people in banking.
pairs.right: I have a lot of contacts in banking.

pairs.left: They used to be called BMG.
I've always wanted to fly a plane.
pairs.right: It's always been my ambition to fly a plane.

pairs.left: She has a great knowledge of finance.

pairs.right: The adverts attracted a lot of attention.

exercises.prompt: Danielle set up another ___ of the company in Manchester, which was run by her brother.
exercises.hint: (an office that is part of the company)
exercises.explanation: A branch is an office that is part of a larger company.

exercises.prompt: The business soon ___ rapidly, and it now has offices in many cities.
exercises.explanation: To expand means to become bigger.

exercises.statement: A shop assistant serves clients, and a lawyer has customers.
exercises.explanation: It is the other way round: shops have customers, and lawyers and accountants have clients.
